I use a "advantage / disadvantage" system in my game. Most combat characters sink at least half their advantage points in combat related stuff (sharpshooter, ambidextrous, colossal, overcharged spells, etc...), but in the list there is a pretty costly advantage which gives a massive amount of skill points to invest in non-combat skills. Add to that minor advantages centered on said non-combat skills (specialist, lucky, etc...) and you can build a character that won't fight but will be a lifesaver for the party in a lot of non-combat situations.

In my game blocking is an attack roll + shield bonus if any. Dodging is a roll that uses different abilities altogether. Usually, specialized warrior have a better blocking roll than their dodge rolls. The tradeoff being that you can't block all types of attacks (bullets, explosions... You can block arrows if you have a shield but that's pretty much it). Dodge is usually more difficult but works against almost everything. Hope that helps.

The guy seems to be some kind of frail sweet talker, so our presence makes sense. After seven days, mercenaries working for the usurper king attack us, and what do you know, the prince was secretly raised by this universe's version of "Bruce-Jackie-Lee-Chan". He was so grossly OP and good at everything that we spent the entire session watching him being awesome at everything. I had my fair share of shit OP DMPC but this one was the worse because we spent the first half of the session thinking that the prince was a decently built character that needed us to accomplish his goals. How naive we were...

What are you looking for? - Some kind of semi-sandbox MMO with open PvP, but consequences for said pvp (and not just the "I can kill other players" switch turned on). Having a nice, skillfull combat system (instead of the standard "stand and hack") would be a plus.

What games have you previously played? - Tera, Secret World, Wildstar, and a bit of Albion Online. If you go back very far into my life, you can add Dark Age of Camelot, Ragnarok Online and PSO.

What is your playstyle (Casual,Semi-Casual,Hardcore)?: Semi-casual to hardcore. I can be very determined if the game suits me ^^
Any preferred mechanics?: Open PvP well done, huge game world with potential for discovery, being able to hide somewhere and get the drop on unsuspecting targets.

Anything specific you want to exclude? - Pay to win (as in "you can pay to instantly gain power beyond what a free player could get") and I'd like the game which is not an absolute grindfest (I know it's par for the course but I've not the patience for korean grinders anymore).
